description: Revalidation in Next.js App Router is the mechanism to update cached data without rebuilds. It includes Time-based Revalidation (automatic after interval) and On-demand Revalidation (purging based on events using tags or paths). This ensures high performance through static delivery while preventing outdated data from persisting indefinitely in production caches.

constraints.title: Use On-demand Revalidation After Data Mutations
constraints.problem: Modifying data via Server Actions or API routes without purging cache tags or paths will cause users to see stale, un-mutated data.
constraints.whyItMatters: Next.js highly caches pages and fetch queries. If a server mutation changes record values in a database, the cache remains unaware of this modification unless `revalidatePath` or `revalidateTag` is explicitly triggered. Failing to clear the cache results in confusing stale user experiences.
forbiddenPatterns: Mutating database tables in Server Actions and redirecting without revalidation
Relying purely on time-based revalidation for user-triggered state modifications
Invoking clientside state mutations without triggering a router refresh or tag purge
allowedPatterns: Invoking revalidateTag('tag-name') after a database query update
Calling revalidatePath('/route-path') after successfully executing a state transition action
Bundling tag purges within Server Actions to ensure database and cache state are in sync
productionRisks: Stale or incorrect data presentation to the user
Form submission loops because changes are not reflected immediately
Cache state mismatch across edge nodes
architectureImplications: Requires coupling mutation points with validation events
Encourages a clean design of tag-based cache architecture across components
optimizationGuidance: Adopt granular tag-based cache configurations (revalidateTag) over full page-level revalidation (revalidatePath) to prevent unnecessary database queries
quickFixes: Add revalidatePath('/route') or revalidateTag('tag') immediately following your database write inside Server Actions
architectureSuggestions: Centralize caching tags inside a constants mapping file to ensure consistent tagging across write and read operations

invalid: export async function action(formData: FormData) { await updateItem(formData.get('id')); redirect('/items'); }
valid: import { revalidatePath } from 'next/cache'; export async function action(formData: FormData) { await updateItem(formData.get('id')); revalidatePath('/items'); redirect('/items'); }

constraints.title: Prevent Caching Mismatch by Synchronizing time-based revalidation tags
constraints.problem: Setting short revalidation intervals on dynamic fetch operations in a static layout will cause rendering mismatches during static generation.
constraints.whyItMatters: If a nested component sets a dynamic fetch timer (e.g. revalidate: 10) but the parent layout is fully static and never revalidated, the dynamic child data might get updated on the server while the static page HTML served to users remains stale, creating caching mismatch boundaries.
forbiddenPatterns: Adding extremely low time-based revalidation options to fetch calls in root layout files
Mixing time-based caching with dynamic route configs without using dynamic configurations
allowedPatterns: Keeping time-based revalidation configs consistent across nested route segments
Declaring export const revalidate = 60; at the top of layout or page component files to enforce global segment behaviors
productionRisks: Inconsistent rendering output on dynamic routing targets
Outdated data presented inside otherwise active dashboard layouts
Unnecessary server load from high frequency cache rebuild schedules
architectureImplications: Requires aligning caching strategies across layout and page tree structures
Pushes revalidation logic up to layout files or down to leaf fetch nodes cleanly
optimizationGuidance: Synchronize child page and parent layout revalidation durations to avoid serving mismatched data states
quickFixes: Add export const revalidate = X; at the page file level to declare page-wide revalidation rules consistently
architectureSuggestions: Enforce layout-wide revalidation values that act as bounds for child pages, avoiding child page caches updating independently from layout shells

invalid: // In component: fetch('/api/data', { next: { revalidate: 5 } }) inside layout.tsx with no revalidate config
valid: // In page.tsx: export const revalidate = 60; export default async function Page() { const data = await fetch('/api/data'); return <main>{data}</main>; }
